summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on hemodialysis via a left femoral tunneled catheter, HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy and opportunistic infection prophylaxis, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was admitted after presenting from dialysis with persistent left-eye blurry vision that began after anesthesia for a recent venogram and with marked post-dialysis hypotension (SBP 58/38) and elevated lactate that improved after a small IV fluid bolus and resumption of midodrine. Ophthalmology found the visual disturbance correctable with a +2.75 lens and a normal dilated fundus exam, consistent with transient loss of accommodation after anesthesia; she had mild improvement and was advised to use over-the-counter reading glasses, follow monocular safety precautions, and obtain outpatient ophthalmology follow-up within one week. Blood cultures remained negative and chest radiograph showed no acute findings while she continued vancomycin with hemodialysis for her recent MRSA catheter-related bacteremia. During the stay she developed sore throat and dysphagia concerning for candidal esophagitis and was started on a 14-day fluconazole course with improvement. Given catheter dysfunction with clotting requiring heparin dwell and concern for thrombosis risk in the setting of complex access and IVC stenosis, she was started on warfarin with plans for INR monitoring during dialysis; left groin swelling was evaluated by ultrasound without fluid collection and improved prior to discharge.
problems: Relative/iatrogenic hypotension after hemodialysis (improved with IV fluids and midodrine)
Left-eye blurry vision likely due to loss of accommodation after anesthesia; monocular precautions and ophthalmology follow-up
Dysphagia/sore throat treated empirically as candidal esophagitis with fluconazole
End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis with complex vascular access; left femoral tunneled catheter dysfunction/clotting risk
Anticoagulation with warfarin initiated for concern of catheter-associated thrombosis risk; INR monitoring planned
Recent MRSA catheter-related bacteremia (continuing vancomycin with hemodialysis); blood cultures negative this admission
HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy and opportunistic infection prophylaxis
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (in sinus rhythm during admission)
Eosinophilia with pruritus/excoriations; Strongyloides antibody negative; dermatology/allergy follow-up planned
